consensus_summary: Primary identification is Jesus’ tomb/grave or the realm of the dead (Sheol/Hades) for the three days between death and resurrection, as the antitype of Jonah; Jerusalem or earthly power is only a minority/rare alternative.
book_summary: Identifies the phrase as Jerusalem, the navel and heart of the land.
consensus_core_identification: Jesus’ grave/tomb or Hades/Sheol (the place of the dead during the three days)
boundary_disagreement: Consensus admits Jerusalem only as a minority chronology-driven alternative while fixing the core as burial/Hades; the book elevates Jerusalem to the sole identification and relegates grave/Hades to a dismissed common view.
material_contradiction: The phrase cannot simultaneously denote both Jerusalem and the tomb/underworld as its primary Matthean referent.
rationale: Minimum cores replace each other: consensus fixes the Jonah-sign referent as the place of Christ’s death/burial sojourn, while the book equates ‘heart of the earth’ with Jerusalem via Ezekiel’s navel language. This is not a boundary refinement of a shared category but a substitution of referents; Jerusalem appears in consensus only as a listed minority alternative, confirming divergence rather than novelty or equivalence.
strongest_objection: Near-universal Christian and scholarly reading of Matt 12:40 treats the phrase as the burial/Hades parallel to Jonah, rendering a Jerusalem identification secondary or forced.
